the blackboard approach can be used to link irrigation and insect pest management expert systems to reschedule conflicting irrigation and insect pest control applications, that rescheduling conflicting irrigation-insecticide applications is sensitive to water stress level, insect damage, rainfall probability, and that the rescheduling decision can be made by the grower, extension agent, or consultant using a blackboard.

the blackboard approach can be successfully used to integrate irrigation and pest management expert systems to resolve conflicting recommendations and that the rescheduling decision is sensitive to water stress level, insect damage level, and rainfall probability.
the blackboard approach can be used to determine the most economically efficient alternative when conflicting irrigation and insect pest management recommendations are made.

the development of a decision support system (DSS) for cotton growers.
developing a methodology for integrating irrigation and pest control recommendations for a given field situation.
the problem of integrating two expert systems to make the most economical reschedulings for conflicting irrigation and pesticide recommendations.

the blackboard approach is an effective tool for resolving conflicts in irrigation and insect management recommendations.
the blackboard approach can be a useful and practical tool to assist growers in making decisions regarding the rescheduling of insecticide and irrigation applications.
the rescheduling decision is a function of insect damage, water stress, and rainfall probability, and the relative economic importance of the two crops being managed.

irrigation scheduling should be based on water stress, insect pest management should be based on pest damage, and both should be based on the rainfall probability.
